c31_startup_investigation.observed_ordering: parity/terminal.py:118-148 launches the child, appends ownership, registers with the process guard, sets up selectors/exit/wake descriptors, then starts the PTY reader. No reader-ready acknowledgement precedes return. A runnable child can issue its initial cursor query before service begins.
c31_startup_investigation.guard_qualification: parity/processes.py:155-172 inspects one PID synchronously, registers identity under a lock and starts a monitor; full discovery is in that monitor before its first event wait. Fresh guards normally have no existing monitor lock contention. Running PTY reads do not acquire the guard lock; monitor/GIL or OS-scheduling effects in the historical failure were not measured. JOBS workers are separate processes.

controlled_diagnostic.purpose: Synthetic offline startup-ordering experiment, not C31 parity execution or acceptance proof
controlled_diagnostic.method: Peer emits a cursor query immediately after raw-mode setup and uses a 100ms protocol receive deadline. An event-controlled barrier holds registration until the peer reports deadline expiry; no arbitrary synchronization sleep.
controlled_diagnostic.after_reader_ready_control: Holding the guard lock after reader/prompt readiness did not prevent correct CPR consumption before lock release. Ordinary next input, shutdown and exact final-state replay passed. This excludes direct running-reader dependence on that lock, not GIL starvation.

c31_startup_investigation.demonstrated: Pre-reader bookkeeping can make a peer deadline expire and trigger fallback while the journal still records the correct reply at the logical query-end offset.
c31_startup_investigation.historical_c31_uncertainty: No timing receipt shows registration actually exceeded the historical C31 deadline. A startup service gap is demonstrated, but historical causation is unproved. Go read-error paths and competing-reader alternatives have not been exhaustively excluded; no new Go defect claimed.
c31_startup_investigation.offset_limitation: parity/terminal.py:218-226 appends a complete read chunk before parsing. Lines183-194 journal replies at logical parsed query-end offsets, then write them. Historical offset857 does not distinguish timely service, buffered query-plus-fallback, delayed write or delayed Go-side consumption.
